[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | One interpretation treats لا as an emphatic extra particle, so the phrase means that they truly are the greatest losers in the afterlife; the following line illustrates جرمت as causing or deserving an outcome.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Lā jarama has dialect variants including lā dhā jarama, lā an dhā jarama, lā ʿan dhā jarama, and lā jar with the mīm dropped through frequent use.

[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Ibn al-Anbari says lā answers unbelievers who think punishment will be diverted, then jarama begins a new clause; jarama either means their unbelief earned punishment or that punishment was made sure, with a poem supporting the latter.
